extracted.intended_audience: Interested persons and stakeholders (manufacturers, trade associations, regulatory commenters, advocacy groups, and members of the public) who may participate in the DOE proposed rulemaking and submit comments or participate in the webinar regarding the proposed withdrawal of the air cleaners coverage determination.
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and procedural/normative criteria for participating in the Department of Energy's notice-and-comment process and webinar for the proposed withdrawal of the coverage determination for air cleaners, including how to submit comments, confidentiality rules, webinar procedures, and the legal/regulatory review standards DOE applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments close date
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be received on or before July 15, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All comments, data, and information regarding this notification of proposed determination must be submitted no later than the date provided in the DATES section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of submission and required docket identifier
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit comments using the Federal eRulemaking Portal at www.regulations.gov under docket number EERE-2025-BT-DET-0016, or by email, postal mail, or hand delivery as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting by email include the docket number EERE-2025-BT-DET-0016 in the subject line. Follow instructions for submitting comments; see ADDRESSES section for full contact details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted electronic file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit electronic comments in WordPerfect, Microsoft Word, PDF, or ASCII file format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the use of special characters or any form of encryption. Comments, data, and other information submitted electronically should be in PDF (preferred), Microsoft Word or Excel, or text (ASCII) file format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document technical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide documents that are not secured, are written in English, and are free of any defects or viruses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents should not contain special characters or any form of encryption and, if possible, should carry the electronic signature of the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations.gov contact information visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations.gov will require your name and contact information; contact information will be viewable to DOE Building Technologies staff only; publicly viewable will be first and last name, organization name, and submitter representative name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your comment is not processed properly because of technical difficulties, DOE will use this information to contact you. If you include contact information in the comment or attachments, that contact information will be publicly viewable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter procedure to avoid public display of contact info
rubrics_metrics.description: If you do not want your personal contact information to be publicly viewable, provide your contact information in a cover letter separate from the comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include your first and last names, email address, telephone number, and optional mailing address in the cover letter. With this instruction followed, the cover letter will not be publicly viewable as long as it does not include any comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Business Information (CBI) submission procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments submitted through regulations.gov cannot be claimed as CBI. To submit information believed to be confidential, send two well-marked copies via email: one labeled 'confidential' and one 'non-confidential' with confidential information deleted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE will make its own determination about the confidential status of the information and treat it accordingly. Do not submit statutory-exempt information through regulations.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Campaign form letters handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit campaign form letters by the originating organization in batches of between 50 to 500 form letters per PDF or as one form letter with a list of supporters' names compiled into one or more PDFs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces comment processing and posting time.

rubrics_metrics.name: No faxes accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: No telefacsimiles ('faxes') will be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use regulations.gov, email, postal mail, or hand delivery as provided in ADDRESSES.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include contact information with each submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Include contact information each time you submit comments, data, documents, and other information to DOE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE will use this information to contact you if your submission is not processed properly. If DOE cannot read your comment and cannot contact you for clarification, DOE may not be able to consider your comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and posting timing for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE processes submissions made through regulations.gov before posting; comments will normally be posted within a few days but may take up to several weeks if large volumes are being processed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the comment tracking number provided after upload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket availability and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The docket for this proposed rulemaking is available at www.regulations.gov and includes Federal Register notices, public meeting attendee lists and transcripts (if held), comments, and other supporting documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The docket web page contains instructions for accessing all documents and a summary of the rulemaking. Not all documents listed may be publicly available if exempt from disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required docket number in submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify submissions by docket number EERE-2025-BT-DET-0016.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including the docket number ensures comments are associated with the correct rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for submitting prepared general statements for distribution at the webinar
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person wishing to make an oral presentation may request an opportunity and must submit a request along with an advance electronic copy of their statement at least one week before the webinar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance copies should be in PDF (preferred), Microsoft Word or Excel, WordPerfect, or text (ASCII) and emailed to the address in ADDRESSES. Include a telephone number for follow-up contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Webinar registration and system compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Webinar registration information, participant instructions, and capabilities available will be published on DOE's website; participants are responsible for ensuring their systems are compatible with the webinar software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the DOE website for registration details and participant instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct and format of the public webinar
rubrics_metrics.description: The webinar will be informal, conference style; DOE will present an overview, allow prepared general statements and encourage discussion; DOE will designate an official to preside and may use a professional facilitator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The meeting is not a judicial or evidentiary public hearing. DOE reserves the right to schedule presentation order, set time limits, accept clarifications, and to announce procedural rules as needed. A court reporter will record proceedings and prepare a transcript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on webinar discussion topics
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall not be discussion of proprietary information, costs or prices, market share, or other commercial matters regulated by U.S. anti-trust laws during the public meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants should avoid discussing proprietary/commercial information that could raise antitrust concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcript availability
rubrics_metrics.description: A transcript of the public meeting will be included in the docket and will be accessible on the DOE website; any person may buy a copy of the transcript from the transcribing reporter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transcripts will be placed in the docket as part of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content topics DOE particularly requests comment on
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE welcomes comments on all aspects of the proposed withdrawal, and is particularly interested in whether withdrawing the coverage determination of air cleaners as a covered product is consistent with the purposes of EPCA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE is also interested in receiving views on other relevant issues that participants believe would affect the tentative conclusions in the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOE policy on public docket inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: It is DOE policy that all comments may be included in the public docket, without change and as received, including any personal information provided (except information deemed exempt from public disclosure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do not want certain personal information public, do not include it in the comment or attached documents; use a separate cover letter for contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory review standard — Executive Order 12866
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should propose or adopt a regulation only upon a reasoned determination that its benefits justify its costs; tailor regulations to impose the least burden consistent with objectives; select approaches that maximize net benefits; specify performance objectives where feasible; and identify/assess available alternatives to direct regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE states this proposed action is consistent with E.O. 12866 and OIRA determined it is not a 'significant regulatory action' under section 3(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory review standard — Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a notice of proposed or final rule is published, agencies must prepare and make available for public comment a regulatory flexibility analysis describing the effect of the rule on small entities, unless certifying no significant impact on a substantial number of small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE concluded the proposed withdrawal would not have a 'significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities' and that an IRFA is not warranted; DOE will transmit its certification and factual statement to the SBA Chief Counsel for Advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proposed action imposes new information or record-keeping requirements, OMB clearance is required under the Paperwork Reduction Act; otherwise clearance is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE asserts this proposed withdrawal imposes no new information or record-keeping requirements; OMB clearance is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE must analyze the proposed action in accordance with NEPA and its implementing regulations, consider applicable categorical exclusions, and complete NEPA review before issuing the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE is considering categorical exclusions (e.g., B5.1) and welcomes comment on their potential application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federalism review — Executive Order 13132
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must examine constitutional/statutory authority for actions that preempt State law or have federalism implications and ensure meaningful input by State and local officials when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE tentatively determined this proposed withdrawal would not have a substantial direct effect on States and no further action under E.O. 13132 is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting and clarity standards — Executive Order 12988
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations should eliminate drafting errors and ambiguity; minimize litigation; provide a clear legal standard for affected conduct; promote simplification and burden reduction; specify preemptive effects, effects on existing law, retroactivity, adequately define key terms, and address other draftsmanship issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE reviewed the proposed withdrawal and determined it meets relevant E.O. 12988 standards to the extent permitted by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates assessment (UMRA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must assess effects on State, local, and Tribal governments and the private sector; if a rule may require expenditures of $100 million or more in any one year, additional analysis and consultation are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE determined this proposed withdrawal does not contain a Federal intergovernmental mandate nor is it expected to require expenditures of $100 million or more; UMRA analytical requirements do not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family Policymaking Assessment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Treasury and General Government Appropriations Act, 1999, agencies must issue a Family Policymaking Assessment for any rule that may affect family well-being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE concluded the proposed withdrawal would not affect family autonomy or integrity and that an assessment is not necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Takings analysis — Executive Order 12630
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must consider whether a proposed action results in takings that might require compensation under the Fifth Amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE determined the proposed withdrawal would not result in takings requiring compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information quality and dissemination review
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should review disseminations of information under OMB and agency information quality guidelines (Treasury and General Government Appropriations Act, 2001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE reviewed the proposed withdrawal under OMB and DOE guidelines and concluded consistency with applicable policies; DOE also references OMB M-19-15 guidance and DOE's updated information quality guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy effects — Executive Order 13211
rubrics_metrics.description: For any 'significant energy action' agencies must prepare a Statement of Energy Effects detailing adverse effects on energy supply, distribution, or use and alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE tentatively determined this rule would not have a significant adverse effect on energy supply, distribution, or use and therefore has not prepared a Statement of Energy Effects, but seeks comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review for influential scientific information
rubrics_metrics.description: Energy conservation standards rulemaking analyses are 'influential scientific information' and should be peer reviewed by qualified specialists per the OMB Information Quality Bulletin for Peer Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE conducted formal peer reviews of its standards development process and engaged the National Academy of Sciences to review analytical methodologies; DOE is evaluating resulting reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive comment focus when coverage withdrawal affects statutory authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should consider that if DOE withdraws the coverage determination, DOE would lack authority to prescribe test procedures and energy conservation standards for air cleaners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because withdrawal affects DOE authority under 42 U.S.C. 6293 and 6295, commenters should consider and comment on the legal and practical consequences of withdrawal (e.g., withdrawing test procedures, certification requirements, and standards).
